pr.title: add_retag: ensure box-to-raw-ptr casts are preserved for Miri
pr.description:
In https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/122233 I added `retag_box_to_raw` not realizing that we can already do `addr_of_mut!(*bx)` to turn a box into a raw pointer without an intermediate reference. We just need to ensure this information is preserved past the ElaborateBoxDerefs pass.

r? @oli-obk
pr.author: RalfJung

processing.reason: The PR's incorrect transformation only omits an `AddRetag`-generated `Retag([raw] ...)` statement for indirect global-Box `AddressOf` while moving `AddRetag` before `ElaborateBoxDerefs`. Retag statements modify Miri aliasing/permission metadata, not computed values. Therefore any observable original-vs-transformed difference requires triggering an aliasing violation (UB) in the historically wrong version, which cannot satisfy the requirement that both versions pass Miri on the tested inputs. There is no defined-execution numeric/boolean/character output difference justified by this PR; fabricating one would be an arbitrary value change unrelated to the historical rewrite.

analysis.originalLogic: `AddRetag` ran after `ElaborateBoxDerefs` and only inserted retags for assignments that pass `needs_retag(place)`. For pointer-creating rvalues it explicitly skipped retagging: `Rvalue::Ref(..) | Rvalue::AddressOf(..) => false` with the rationale "Ptr-creating operations already do their own internal retagging, no need to also add a retag statement." The pass pipeline comment stated only: "`AddRetag` needs to run after `ElaborateDrops`. Otherwise it should run fairly late, but before optimizations begin." `ElaborateBoxDerefs` therefore ran before `AddRetag` and desugared Box derefs to direct use of the inner raw pointer.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to emit no retag statement for an `Rvalue::AddressOf` assignment (treating all AddressOf as already self-retagging). For `std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(**x)` where `x: &mut Box<i32>`, the Box-to-raw pointer cast thus lost the `Retag([raw] _0)` information after `ElaborateBoxDerefs` had rewritten the Box deref to the inner raw pointer. In Miri this made the cast a NOP "when the original pointer is already raw", losing the required shared/Unique permission effect. The corrected transformation emits `Some(RetagKind::Raw)` for `Rvalue::AddressOf` when `place.is_indirect_first_projection() && body.local_decls[place.local].ty.is_box_global(tcx)`, moves `AddRetag` before `ElaborateBoxDerefs`, and permits `RetagKind::Raw` through the validator (previously `RetagKind::Raw | RetagKind::TwoPhase` was forbidden).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR assignments of raw-pointer type produced from a Box, in particular `addr_of_mut!(*box)` / `std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(**x)` where the Box is behind a reference or otherwise indirect, with a global allocator Box (`is_box_global`). Also includes the ordering relationship between `AddRetag` and `ElaborateBoxDerefs` for all runtime-lowered MIR. Not concerned with two-phase borrows.
analysis.summary: Historical `AddRetag` skipped all `Rvalue::AddressOf` assignments, so Box-to-raw-pointer casts such as `addr_of_mut!(**box)` lost their `Retag([raw])`, and running after `ElaborateBoxDerefs` erased the Box origin. The fix adds a Raw retag for indirect global-Box AddressOf and runs `AddRetag` before `ElaborateBoxDerefs`; regression is checked via a SimplifyCfg MIR dump.
analysis.trigger: An assignment whose rvalue is `Rvalue::AddressOf(_mutbl, place)`, where `place` is an indirect dereference and the local's type is a global-allocator Box. Without the fix no `Retag([raw] ...)` statement is generated, and `ElaborateBoxDerefs` has already replaced the Box deref with direct manipulation of the inner raw pointer.
preconditions: `AddRetag` must run on runtime-lowered MIR after `ElaborateDrops` but before `ElaborateBoxDerefs`
The AddressOf base place must be indirect (`is_indirect_first_projection()`), i.e. dereferencing the Box local
The Box local type must satisfy `is_box_global(tcx)` (global allocator only; generic/custom allocator code is deliberately not retagged)
The validator must allow explicit `RetagKind::Raw`; it previously forbade `RetagKind::Raw | RetagKind::TwoPhase`
A retag for `Rvalue::Ref` must still be skipped, while other rvalues use `needs_retag(place)`
pitfalls: Do not conflate the AddressOf case with Ref: Ref still gets no added retag, but AddressOf-of-Box needs `RetagKind::Raw`
Pass ordering matters: moving `AddRetag` after `ElaborateBoxDerefs` loses the Box origin because Box derefs desugar to raw pointers
The `is_box_global` check is acknowledged as a hack: if code is generic over the allocator no retag is added, for Stacked Borrows compatibility with custom allocator code
The fixed implementation changes Miri diagnostics from `SharedReadWrite retag` to `Unique retag` in newtype retagging tests, so stderr expectations are part of the behavior
The regression test is a MIR-dump test (`EMIT_MIR`), not a compile-pass/execution test; it asserts the raw retag survives to `SimplifyCfg-pre-optimizations` for both panic-abort and panic-unwind
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused MIR-dump regression test in `tests/mir-opt/retag.rs` with `// EMIT_MIR retag.box_to_raw_mut.SimplifyCfg-pre-optimizations.after.mir` and function `fn box_to_raw_mut(x: &mut Box<i32>) -> *mut i32 { std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(**x) }`. Check the `SimplifyCfg-pre-optimizations` output contains the raw assignment followed by the retag, for both panic strategies: `_0 = &raw mut (*_3);` then `Retag([raw] _0);`. Diff the fixed vs. historically wrong pipeline by running `AddRetag` after vs. before `ElaborateBoxDerefs` and confirming the pre-fix output lacks the Raw retag. Also inspect Miri Stacked Borrows expectations such as `newtype_retagging.stack.stderr` changing from `SharedReadWrite retag` to `Unique retag`.
evidence: We just need to ensure this information is preserved past the ElaborateBoxDerefs pass.
